+//! The thread-cycle record over a thread's laid passes (issue #34,
+//! filled from the infeed plan since #416, stating exactly the laid
+//! passes in the cycle's terms since #417): the numbers a lathe
+//! control's multi-pass threading cycle needs, read off the built path
+//! and the plan that laid it.
+//!
+//! Provenance: the cycle quantities (first-pass and minimum depth,
+//! finish allowance, infeed angle, spring passes) as public lathe
+//! programming references list them for a multi-pass threading cycle
+//! (GSK988TA manual G76, Fanuc-compatible; LinuxCNC G76) - behaviour
+//! only; our own mapping from our pass plan.
+
+use crate::cl::{MoveKind, ThreadCycle, Toolpath};
+
+use super::infeed::{DepthSchedule, InfeedMethod, Pass, ThreadInfeed};
+use super::thread::ThreadParams;
+
+/// Attach the record over `moves[first..=last]`, stating the very
+/// passes laid (issue #417) in a lathe cycle's own terms, so a control
+/// running the cycle cuts what was verified:
+/// - first depth: the first pass's;
+/// - minimum depth: the rung for a constant-depth ladder (a minimum
+///   equal to the first depth makes the cycle's sqrt(n) steps all the
+///   rung), the plan's own for a constant-area one;
+/// - finish allowance: the depth of the finishing pass - the first pass
+///   at the root - below the pass before it. A cycle roughs to
+///   `height - allowance` and then finishes at the root; stating 0 when
+///   the last roughing rung IS the root would have the control cut that
+///   root twice (one pass the verdict never saw). A one-pass thread
+///   states the whole height, which no cycle can rough to.
+/// - infeed angle: the INCLUDED angle of the compound infeed (twice the
+///   flank angle; 0 radial); alternating infeed sets `alternating`;
+/// - a plan that repeats every roughing depth (#418) sets
+///   `repeat_each_depth` - no single cycle states it; likewise a plan
+///   with chip-break dips (#419) sets `chip_break_dips`.
+///
+/// A span the builder did not lay as planned gets no record; the
+/// passes still post.
+#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
+pub(super) fn attach_cycle(
+    path: &mut Toolpath,
+    first: usize,
+    last: usize,
+    ref_top: f64,
+    root: f64,
+    p: &ThreadParams,
+    plan: &ThreadInfeed,
+    passes: &[Pass],
+) {
+    const NONE: &str = "threading: the passes did not lay as planned - no thread cycle record";
+    let infeed_angle = match plan.method {
+        InfeedMethod::Radial => 0.0,
+        InfeedMethod::Flank | InfeedMethod::Alternating => 2.0 * plan.flank_angle,
+    };
+    let (Some(m0), Some(end)) = (path.moves.get(first), last.checked_sub(1).and_then(|i| path.moves.get(i)))
+    else {
+        path.notes.push(NONE.into());
+        return;
+    };
+    let height = ref_top - root;
+    let first_depth = passes.first().map_or(p.depth, |q| ref_top - q.tip);
+    // The finishing pass is the first one standing at the root; its
+    // depth is measured from the pass before it (the whole height when
+    // it is the first pass).
+    let at_root = passes.iter().position(|q| q.tip <= root + super::revolve::HAIR);
+    let finish_allowance = match at_root {
+        Some(0) | None => height,
+        Some(i) => passes.get(i - 1).map_or(height, |q| q.tip - root),
+    };
+    let min_depth = match plan.schedule {
+        DepthSchedule::ConstantDepth => p.infeed.min(height),
+        DepthSchedule::ConstantArea => plan.min_depth,
+    };
+    let rec = ThreadCycle {
+        start: m0.to,
+        end: end.to,
+        major_diameter: 2.0 * ref_top,
+        minor_diameter: 2.0 * root,
+        lead: p.pitch,
+        height,
+        first_depth,
+        min_depth,
+        finish_allowance,
+        infeed_angle,
+        spring_passes: plan.spring_passes,
+        pull_out: 0.0,
+        alternating: plan.method == InfeedMethod::Alternating,
+        repeat_each_depth: plan.repeat_each_depth,
+        chip_break_dips: plan.dips.is_on(),
+        first,
+        last,
+        hand: p.hand,
+    };
+    if m0.kind == MoveKind::Rapid && rec.is_sane(&path.moves) {
+        path.threads.push(rec);
+    } else {
+        path.notes.push(NONE.into());
+    }
+}

+## #416 - threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
+
+- **Chosen:** a Threading op carries an infeed plan
+  (`turning::ThreadInfeed`, op field `infeed_plan`): method (radial,
+  flank, alternating flank) with a flank angle, depth schedule (constant
+  depth, constant area), minimum depth per pass, finish allowance and
+  spring passes. The kernel (`turning::infeed`) lays the pass list from
+  it; `thread_planned_in` cuts it; `thread_in` is the default plan.
+- **The existing `infeed` field is the first-pass depth.** In a
+  constant-depth ladder the first pass and every pass are the same
+  number (LinuxCNC G76 J with R1.0 works the same way), so a separate
+  first-depth field would only add a cross-field rule. In a constant-area
+  ladder `infeed` is Δd and pass n reaches Δd·√n. Dropped: a second
+  `first_depth` field.
+- **Defaults reproduce today exactly.** The default plan (radial,
+  constant depth, allowance 0, 0 spring passes) calls the same
+  `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0.0)` the kernel called before,
+  every station is `c_last - 0.0` (the chuck-ward start #629 set), and the
+  record is filled the same way.
+  The existing golden suites (motion `turning_thread`,
+  `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76` with its
+  G76 golden, `lathe_field_tools`, `project_roundtrip`) pass with no golden
+  touched. The stamp digests the plan only when it is not the default, so
+  every cached thread stays fresh. The project key is written only when
+  not the default, so no version step (the approach / holes precedent).
+  A file written with a non-default plan and opened in an older build
+  loses the plan and cuts the radial ladder. That is not a gouge, and it
+  is the price the additive law always pays.
+- **Constant-area schedule:** cumulative depth `max(Δd·√n, previous +
+  Δdmin)`, the last roughing pass clamped to `root + allowance`. The
+  clamp is on each pass's own travel. The public G76 references define
+  Δdmin as the minimum cutting travel of a pass (GSK988TA manual G76,
+  Fanuc-compatible). The manual's OCR'd formula fragment can also be read
+  as clamping against the unclamped previous depth, but that reading would
+  let a pass travel less than Δdmin, against the parameter's own
+  definition. Recorded for #417.
+- **Finish allowance:** roughing stops at `root + allowance`, then one
+  finishing pass at the root. 0 means the last roughing pass is the root
+  itself (today's ladder). **Spring passes:** repeats of the root pass,
+  capped at 98 (the two-digit finishing count of the lathe cycles, one
+  of them the finish).
+- **Flank infeed geometry and the safety law:** each pass's start moves
+  along its travel by `-(tip - root)·tan(θ)`. Shallower passes stand
+  behind the lattice centre, deeper ones move toward the direction of
+  travel, so the leading flank cuts and the trailing flank rides the cut
+  flank. The finishing pass and the spring passes stand on the lattice
+  itself. A pass h above the root shifted by h·tan(θ) keeps both flanks
+  inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ A/2 (A = the insert's included
+  angle). So θ > A/2 is refused by name at Create, Paste, Edit and retype
+  (`thread_gate`, which reads the named insert's tip angle), and again by
+  the kernel at Generate (a later tool change meets it there). The shift
+  moves the pass start only. The lead is unchanged, and every pass starts
+  on the meridian, so the helix phase relative to the spindle is the
+  lattice's.
+- **Shift sign:** LinuxCNC's G76 reference says a positive compound
+  angle "causes the leading edge of the tool to cut more heavily". The
+  plan follows that sign. Containment holds either way, so the sign is a
+  chip-control question, not a gouge question.
+- **Alternating flank:** each roughing pass alternates the sign of the
+  same shift (tip zig-zags between the two lines through the root at ±θ).
+  Containment is the same proof. There is no single compound angle, so
+  the path carries no thread-cycle record (a note says so). The passes
+  post as G32. With G76 chosen, the post refuses on the missing record;
+  #417 gives the record a flag and the refusal its own name.
+- **A flank plan's record starts at the crest's flank station:** a rapid
+  at the clearance radius to `c_last + height·tan(θ)` opens the span, so
+  the record's start is where a pass at the crest would start, and pass n
+  is at `start - depth_n·tan(θ)`. Only flank plans get this extra rapid,
+  so the radial path is unchanged.
+- **The verdict reads the laid geometry:** `thread_warnings` takes each
+  pass's station from its own plunge and arc endpoints. So a shifted pass
+  is judged where it stands (pinned by `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass`,
+  which moves a pass past the half-angle and is convicted). The lathe
+  stock simulation does not simulate threads (it refuses them by name, as
+  before).
+- **Rebuilt on #629's chuck-ward ladder (merge of main, 2026-11-10):**
+  #629 reversed every pass to run toward the chuck (enter at the top
+  lattice point `c_last`, fall to `c_first`), gave the arcs the thread's
+  hand and put the hand on the record. The plan rides that ladder
+  unchanged: `shift` is still measured along the pass's travel, and the
+  travel is now -Z, so a pass's station offset is `-shift` - shallower
+  flank passes stand toward the free end (+Z), the leading flank (the
+  chuck side) cuts. Kept as main had it: the direction, `c_last`, the
+  hand's arc sense and `ThreadCycle.hand` (filled from `p.hand` in
+  `thread_cycle::attach_cycle`). The OpParams/DTO/digest carry both
+  `infeed_plan` and `hand`; the hand is digested after the plan, as
+  main wrote it for both hands. Considered and dropped: keeping the
+  plan's stations measured from `c_first` - that would undo #629's
+  direction, a P0 safety fix.
+- **Defaults of the new numbers:** flank angle 29.5° (the modified-flank
+  figure the tooling guides give for 60° forms; read only by flank and
+  alternating) and minimum depth 0.05 mm (the guides' smallest
+  recommended infeed; read only by constant area).
+- **Considered and dropped:** a per-depth repeat pass (#418) and in-pass
+  chip-break dips (#419) are their own issues. Haas-style one-block G76
+  P1-P4 has no post here.
+- **Cost to change later:** the plan is one struct with a DTO mirror. A
+  new method or schedule is an enum arm in both, plus a `passes` arm.

+## #417 - G76 output states the passes that were verified
+
+- **Chosen:** the thread-cycle record states the laid passes in the
+  cycle's own terms. With `G76Cycle` the two blocks
+  `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F` describe the
+  same passes the kernel laid and the verdict judged:
+  - dd = the first pass's depth;
+  - dmin = the rung (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
+  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
+  - m = 1 + spring passes;
+  - a = twice the flank angle.
+
+  Anything the cycle cannot state is refused by name in the post:
+  - alternating flank infeed (a new `alternating` flag on the record);
+  - a flank angle whose double is not 0/29/30/55/60/80 (the existing
+    check; a 29.5° modified flank is a=59 and refused);
+  - a one-pass thread (d would equal k).
+- **The control's schedule, as modelled** (GSK988TA manual G76,
+  Fanuc-compatible; LinuxCNC G76 for the flank sign):
+  - roughing pass n reaches `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to `k - d`;
+  - the first finishing pass cuts d to k, and m - 1 more repeat k;
+  - with a ≠ 0, each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z from the
+    start point.
+
+  The clamp reading follows the manual's definition of Q(Δdmin) as the
+  *minimum cutting travel* of a pass. Its OCR'd formula can be read as
+  clamping against the unclamped previous depth, but then a pass could
+  travel less than dmin, which contradicts that definition.
+  `lathe_post_g76_schedule` computes this schedule from the posted words
+  and checks it against the laid passes' depths and stations to within
+  1 µm, for a constant-area flank thread (new golden `thread_g76_area.nc`)
+  and for the default thread.
+- **The existing mismatch, and the honest fix (golden changed):** the
+  research comment on #363 said the control cut a decreasing ladder
+  because we posted `Q = infeed` as the first depth. That is not what
+  happens: dmin was also posted as the infeed, so the clamp makes every
+  step the rung, and the control's roughing matched ours. The real
+  mismatch was `R0`. With d = 0 the control roughs all the way to k
+  (0.4, 0.8, 1.2) and then cuts its finishing pass at k again, which is a
+  fourth pass at the root that the verdict never judged. It is not a
+  gouge, because it is the same root, but it is not what was verified.
+  The fix: R states the finishing pass's own depth, the last rung's 0.4.
+  The control then roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2, the three

+  `... R0.4`, and nothing else in it changes. The G32 output and the

+  The motion `turning_thread_cycle` test now pins `finish_allowance`
+  0.4 instead of 0.
+- **Why not the other way round** (add a root pass so R0 is honest):
+  that would change the default G32 output and every pass the verdict
+  judges, which #416 promised not to do, and it would add a spring pass
+  nobody asked for.
+- **A flank record starts at the crest's flank station** (from #416):
+  the posted `G00 X Z` start is `c_first - k·tan(θ)`, so the control's
+  pass n (at `start + depth_n·tan(a/2)`) lands where the kernel laid it,

+- **Not verifiable from the sources read, flagged for Hub / machine:**
+  - The sign of the per-pass Z shift. We follow LinuxCNC's "positive
+    angle, leading edge cuts more heavily": deeper passes move in the
+    direction of travel.
+  - Whether the control also shifts each pass's END Z, or ends every

+  None of these moves the finished form; all three should be checked in

+- **Record plumbing:** `ThreadCycle.alternating` and `ThreadRec.alternating`.
+  The stream line writes `ALT 1` only when set (absent reads 0), so

+- **Cost to change later:** a dialect with an alternating cycle (Haas
+  one-block G76 P2/P4, a LinuxCNC post) reads the same flag. Changing

+- **The Tormach (LinuxCNC) G76 reads the new finish allowance too**

+- **TH1 Stale after a save/load is a main defect** (not this PR's data):

+## #418 - threading: repeat each roughing depth ("spring at each depth")
+
+- **Chosen:** a bool on the infeed plan, `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`
+  (default off). When on, `ThreadInfeed::passes` follows every pass that
+  stands above the root with an identical copy of itself, so each
+  roughing depth is cut twice before the next one. Dropped: a count
+  (2, 3, ... cuts per depth). The issue asks for "twice", and nothing in
+  the research asks for more. If a count is ever needed, the bool
+  becomes a `u32` with a DTO default of 1, and the absent key still
+  reads as off.
+- **The repeat is the same pass, so it cannot gouge.** It is pushed as
+  the same `Pass { tip, shift }`, and the kernel lays it from the same
+  lattice start (`c_first + shift`) with the same lead, so the repeat
+  has the same tip, the same station and the same helix phase. Its
+  moves are identical to the first cut's
+  (`a_repeat_is_the_same_pass_on_every_method_and_the_judge_stays_silent`
+  compares the move spans for every method and schedule). The verdict
+  judges the laid passes, the repeats included, and stays silent.
+- **Alternating infeed counts depths, not cuts.** The side flips once per
+  depth, so a repeated depth keeps its side. If the flip counted cuts,
+  the "repeat" would cut the other flank, which would make it a
+  different pass.
+- **What gets repeated:** every pass whose tip is above the root
+  (`tip > root + HAIR`). The finishing pass and the spring passes at
+  the root are not repeated: those passes already exist as spring
+  passes and have their own count. With no finish allowance, the last
+  rung is the root, so it is the finishing pass and is cut once
+  (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.2).
+- **G76 refuses by name.** A one-block cycle cuts each depth once, so
+  the record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag. This follows #417's
+  `alternating` precedent: the stream writes `REP 1` only when the flag
+  is set, the post property is `RepeatEachDepth`, and the project cache
+  key is written only when set. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses
+  "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle". The kernel does not
+  refuse, because the G32 / G76 choice is a document post option, not
+  an op parameter. The refusal therefore happens where that choice is
+  known, the same way alternating infeed is refused.
+- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With the default off:
+  - the kernel lays the same passes;
+  - the stamp writes no extra byte (one byte, `0xD5`, only when the
+    flag is set, inside the non-default branch);
+  - the project's `infeed_plan` key and the record key are absent;
+  - the stream writes no `REP` word.
+
+  No golden changed. A #416 file with a non-default plan and no
+  `repeat_each_depth` key loads with the repeat off (serde default).
+- **UI:** one checkbox row, "Repeat each depth", on the Passes tab
+  after "Spring passes". Its tooltip says G32 only, says G76 refuses
+  it, and notes that tooling makers recommend against routine spring
+  passes.
+- **Cost to change later:** one field in the plan and in its DTO, one
+  flag on the record. A dialect with a per-depth repeat would read the
+  same flag. No public cycle we read has one.

+## #419 - threading: in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
+
+- **The citation came first, as the issue required.** The primary Fanuc
+  source is the *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe
+  System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II. I read it from a public mirror of
+  Fanuc's PDF:
+  https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078.
+  The sections it gives us:
+  - §3.4 "Continuous Threading" (p. 34): consecutive threading blocks
+    keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between
+    blocks", and threads whose "lead and shape change midway" may be
+    cut that way.
+  - §3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6 (p. 32): a threading
+    block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for
+    detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
+  - §3.2, pp. 29-31: G32 cuts tapers (worked example `G32 X41.0 Z29.0
+    F3.5`). Up to a 45° taper the lead F is taken along Z, and past 45°
+    along X.
+
+  The Haas lathe G32 reference (sync "stays in effect for each
+  subsequent G32 line") corroborates this. LinuxCNC G33 is still
+  unconfirmed: its reference page does not say whether a chained G33
+  waits for the index again. The citation sits in the header of
+  `fanuc-lathe.cps`, beside the new flag.
+- **Chosen: a variable-radius thread half-turn as the new CL segment.** A
+  dip is an XY half-turn about the spindle axis whose end radius differs
+  from its start radius. Its axial travel is still exactly half a lead,
+  so the CL needs no new move kind. The arc struct already allows
+  unequal end radii: chords take the larger radius, which is the
+  shallower side and so conservative, and the timeline length is
+  unchanged. Dropped: a new `MoveKind` or a per-move "synchronized"
+  field. Either would touch every CL consumer (text, dump, project,
+  sim, verify) and carry the same two endpoints anyway.
+- **What marks a dip: the thread record plus a section PARAM.**
+  `ThreadCycle.chip_break_dips` is written as `DIP 1` in the stream,
+  property `ChipBreakDips`, and as a project cache key only when set
+  (the #417 / #418 precedent). Whenever a path's record carries that
+  flag, the dump also writes `PARAM ChipBreakDips 1.000000`. The engine
+  refuses that PARAM by name for any script that does not declare
+  `continuousThreading = true`, the same way `liveTooling` works. If
+  dips are on and the record cannot be attached, the kernel refuses, so
+  a dip is never laid unmarked. Dropped: having the engine spot dips by
+  geometry (unequal arc radii). Fitted milling arcs can differ in
+  radius by up to their tolerance, so that check would refuse good mill
+  programs.
+- **Only fanuc-lathe declares the flag.** Each other post needs its own
+  manual citation first. The mill posts never see dips, because the
+  engine refuses the section.
+- **Dips are radial, not along the flank vector.** The issue says "along
+  the infeed vector", and for radial infeed that is the same thing. For
+  flank or alternating infeed, a radial lift keeps the pass's own
+  station, and a V on the same station with a higher tip lies inside
+  the V the pass already cuts. So a dip can never take more than the
+  pass, whatever the infeed. A lift along the flank would shift the
+  station, so the dip's Z travel would no longer be half a lead and F
+  would no longer be the lead. Dropped for that reason.
+- **Parameters (`ThreadInfeed.dips`):**
+  - interval: axial, rounded up to half-turns, at least two leads, and
+    at least one whole lead longer than the dip. 0 means off, which is
+    the default.
+  - height: radial, at least 0.01 mm so a post can tell it from the
+    micron grid, and at most every dipped pass's depth of cut.
+  - length: axial, out-ramp to in-ramp, rounded up to half-turns. It is
+    never shorter than its two ramps; 0 gives the shortest dip.
+
+  Each ramp takes the fewest half-turns that keep the diameter change
+  0.01 mm under the axial travel. That stays under 45° whether the
+  control measures the taper in radius or in diameter, and the margin
+  keeps the post's micron-rounded check on the same side as the
+  kernel's. Dips start at one interval, then every interval after that.
+  A dip must end before the last lead, and the first lead is always
+  clear, because the interval is at least two leads.
+- **Where dips may stand:** roughing passes only. Not on the finishing
+  pass or the spring passes at the root, not on the repeat of a depth
+  (#418: a repeat exists to clean that depth whole), and not in a
+  chain's first or last lead.
+- **Refusals by name:**
+  - At the command door and the kernel: a dip higher than the first
+    pass's depth, too small, or not a length.
+  - At the kernel: higher than a later roughing pass's own depth (the
+    message names the shallowest), an interval that leaves no whole
+    lead between dips, a thread too short for any dip outside its first
+    and last lead, and a thread with no roughing pass (a one-pass
+    thread).
+  - At the post: G76 chosen ("chip-break dips are not a G76 cycle"), and
+    a post without the flag (engine).
+  - In `fanuc-lathe.cps`, as a backstop per segment: a dip that does not
+    continue a G32 chain (a fresh G32 would wait for the index and
+    restart mid-thread), one steeper than 45°, and one deeper than the
+    chain's plunge.
+- **Refused versus silently skipped.** A thread too short for a dip, or
+  one with no roughing pass, is refused rather than laid with no dips.
+  The user asked for chip breaking, and a silent no-op is a wrong
+  answer they would only find at the machine.
+- **The verdict judges the dip geometry.** `thread_warnings` now also
+  re-reads each chain, meaning a plunge followed by its unbroken
+  half-turns. It convicts, with a gouge at the move:
+  - a half-turn whose axial advance differs from the chain's first
+    (the phase law);
+  - any half-turn standing deeper than the plunge;
+  - a variable-radius half-turn that is steeper than 45°, inside the
+    first or last lead, or on the deepest chain (the finishing or
+    spring passes).
+
+  A gouge holds the post. The existing wave judge reads a dip
+  half-turn at its deeper end, and that end is never deeper than the
+  pass. With the new laws switched off, the first-lead conviction test
+  fails, so the convictions come from these laws and not from the wave
+  judge (checked by hand while writing the PR).
+- **Simulation is unchanged.** The lathe stock simulation refuses threads
+  by name, as it did before. Dipped threads are covered by the same
+  refusal, so nothing new is shown wrongly.
+- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off:
+  - each half-turn's radius is the pass's tip, copied bit for bit;
+  - there is no stamp byte (`0xD6` plus three numbers only when dips are
+    on);
+  - the `dips` key is written only when not the default, and the record
+    key only when set;
+  - there is no `DIP` word and no PARAM.
+
+  No existing golden moved. The new golden is
+  `nc/fanuc-lathe/thread_g32_dips.nc`.
+- **File sizes:** `post/engine.rs` (439 lines before this PR) and
+  `post/mod.rs` (523 before) were already over the 400-line target, and
+  this PR adds 4 and 6 lines to them. The refusal text lives in
+  `cnc_thread.rs` to keep the growth small. Splitting the engine is its
+  own refactor.
+- **Cost to change later:**
+  - A LinuxCNC or other post sets `continuousThreading = true` once it
+    has its own citation.
+  - A flank-vector lift would need F recomputed per segment.
+  - A dip count or placement other than "every interval" changes only
+    `thread_dips::radii`.
+- **Rebased onto #629's chuck-ward ladder (merge of the refreshed #418
+  stack).** Every pass now enters at the free-end lattice point and
+  travels -Z. The dip layout is counted in half-turns along the pass's
+  own travel, from its entry, so it carries over unchanged: the first
+  lead after the entry and the last lead before the retract stay whole,
+  and the dips stand mirrored in Z against the old +Z layout. The hand
+  check (#629) runs on every half-turn before the dip logic, in both
+  the kernel verdict and the lathe script, so a dip ramp is held to the
+  hand like any other half-turn. Dropped: keeping dips measured from
+  the chuck end, which would have put the "first lead" law on the exit
+  end of the pass.
